Neumann 问题：$$\begin{cases}\Delta u=0, & x\in\Omega,\\ \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial n}=g, & x\in\partial\Omega,\end{cases}$$ 其中 $n$ 为外法向。对 $\Delta u=0$ 在 $\Omega$ 上积分并用散度定理：$$0=\int_\Omega\Delta u\,dA=\oint_{\partial\Omega}\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}\,ds=\oint_{\partial\Omega}g\,ds.$$ 故 $\oint_{\partial\Omega}g\,ds=0$ 是解存在的必要条件；在边界足够光滑时它也是充分条件。若 $u$ 是解，则 $u+C$ 对任意常数 $C$ 也是解，所以 Neumann 问题只能唯一到相差一个常数。不能把 Neumann 数据当成 Dirichlet 数据：前者给法向导数，后者给函数值，唯一性结论也不同。

基本解与 Green 函数：$$\Gamma(x)= rac1{2\pi}\ln|x|,\qquad x
e0,$$ 在 $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ 上调和，并在分布意义下满足 $\Delta\Gamma=\delta_0$。对区域 $\Omega$，取 Green 函数 $$G(x,y)=\Gamma(x-y)-h_y(x),$$ 其中 $h_y$ 在 $\Omega$ 内调和、在边界上等于 $\Gamma(x-y)$，于是 $G(x,y)=0$ 当 $x\in\partial\Omega$，且 $G$ 对称。由 Green 第二公式，调和函数 $u$ 可由边界值表示：$$u(x)=\oint_{\partial\Omega}g(y) rac{\partial G}{\partial
u_y}(x,y)\,ds_y.$$ 在半径 $R$ 的圆盘上取镜像点构造 $G$，得到 Poisson 公式 $$ egin{aligned}u(r,	heta)&= rac{R^2-r^2}{2\pi}\&\quad	imes\int_0^{2\pi} rac{g(\varphi)\,d\varphi}{R^2-2Rr\cos(	heta-\varphi)+r^2},\&\qquad 0\le r<R,\end{aligned}$$ 它在 $r	o R^-$ 时连续地取到连续的边界数据 $g$。符号约定：这里取 $\Gamma=+ rac1{2\pi}\ln r$、$
u$ 为外法向；若基本解取相反符号，表示式也要相应变号。
derivationEn: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded connected open set and $u\in C^2(\Omega)$. Laplace's equation is $$\Delta u=\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial y^2}=0,$$ and its solutions are harmonic functions. For example, $u=x^2-y^2$ has $u_{xx}=2$ and $u_{yy}=-2$, so $\Delta u=0$; $u=\ln r$ for $r>0$ is also harmonic; while $u=x^2+y^2$ has $\Delta u=4$ and is not. In the second-order classification $A=C=1,B=0$, so $\Delta=B^2-AC=-1<0$ and the equation is elliptic. It contains no time derivative, takes boundary data only, and describes steady states.

Mean value property: let $B(x_0,R)\subset\Omega$ and let $u$ be harmonic. For $0<r<R$ define the circle average $$A(r)= rac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}u(x_0+r\cos	heta,y_0+r\sin	heta)\,d	heta.$$ Then $$ egin{aligned}A'(r)&= rac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}
abla u\cdot e_r\,d	heta\&= rac1{2\pi r}\int_{\partial B(x_0,r)} rac{\partial u}{\partial
u}\,ds\&= rac1{2\pi r}\int_{B(x_0,r)}\Delta u\,dA=0,\end{aligned}$$ where $
u$ is the outward normal and the last step uses the divergence theorem. Hence $A(r)$ is constant; as $r	o0^+$, continuity of $u$ gives $A(r)	o u(x_0)$, so $u(x_0)=A(r)$. Integrating $2\pi rA(r)$ over $0<r<R$ gives the disk average $$u(x_0)= rac1{\pi R^2}\int_{B(x_0,R)}u\,dA.$$ The hypotheses are that the closed ball lies in $\Omega$ and $u\in C^2$, so that the divergence theorem applies.

Maximum principle: let $\Omega$ be bounded and connected, and let $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ be harmonic and nonconstant. If $u$ attains its maximum $M$ at an interior point $x_0\in\Omega$, choose $r>0$ with $B(x_0,r)\subset\Omega$. The mean value property gives $$M=u(x_0)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}u(x_0+re^{i\theta})\,d\theta.$$ The integrand is at most $M$ everywhere, yet its average equals $M$, so $u\equiv M$ on that circle. Since $r$ can be arbitrarily small, $u$ is identically $M$ in a neighborhood of $x_0$; by connectedness of $\Omega$ and continuity of $u$, the nonempty set $\{u=M\}$ is both open and closed, hence equals $\Omega$, contradicting that $u$ is nonconstant. Therefore the maximum is attained only on the boundary; applying the same argument to $-u$ shows the same for the minimum.

Dirichlet uniqueness and stability: consider $$\begin{cases}\Delta u=0, & x\in\Omega,\\ u=g, & x\in\partial\Omega,\end{cases}$$ with $g$ continuous and bounded. If $u_1,u_2$ are two $C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ solutions, set $w=u_1-u_2$. Then $\Delta w=0$ and $w|_{\partial\Omega}=0$; by the maximum principle, both the maximum and minimum of $w$ on $\overline\Omega$ occur on the boundary and equal $0$, so $w\equiv0$ and the solution is unique. Moreover, applying the maximum principle to $\pm u$ gives $$\sup_{\Omega}|u|\le\sup_{\partial\Omega}|g|,$$ so small changes in the boundary data produce small changes in the solution: the solution depends continuously on the data. Existence can be proved under sufficient boundary regularity (for instance $C^2$) or by a Perron-type argument on regular domains; uniqueness and stability do not depend on the existence proof.

Neumann problem: $$\begin{cases}\Delta u=0, & x\in\Omega,\\ \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial n}=g, & x\in\partial\Omega,\end{cases}$$ where $n$ is the outward normal. Integrating $\Delta u=0$ over $\Omega$ and using the divergence theorem, $$0=\int_\Omega\Delta u\,dA=\oint_{\partial\Omega}\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}\,ds=\oint_{\partial\Omega}g\,ds.$$ Thus $\oint_{\partial\Omega}g\,ds=0$ is necessary for existence, and it is also sufficient when the boundary is sufficiently smooth. If $u$ is a solution, so is $u+C$ for every constant $C$; hence a Neumann problem determines the solution only up to an additive constant. Neumann data must not be treated as Dirichlet data: the former prescribe the normal derivative, the latter the function values, and their uniqueness statements differ.

Fundamental solution and Green's function: $$\Gamma(x)= rac1{2\pi}\ln|x|,\qquad x
e0,$$ is harmonic on $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ and satisfies $\Delta\Gamma=\delta_0$ in the distributional sense. For a domain $\Omega$, take the Green function $$G(x,y)=\Gamma(x-y)-h_y(x),$$ where $h_y$ is harmonic in $\Omega$ and equals $\Gamma(x-y)$ on the boundary, so that $G(x,y)=0$ for $x\in\partial\Omega$ and $G$ is symmetric. Green's second identity represents a harmonic function by its boundary values: $$u(x)=\oint_{\partial\Omega}g(y) rac{\partial G}{\partial
u_y}(x,y)\,ds_y.$$ On a disk of radius $R$, constructing $G$ by the reflection point yields Poisson's formula $$ egin{aligned}u(r,	heta)&= rac{R^2-r^2}{2\pi}\&\quad	imes\int_0^{2\pi} rac{g(\varphi)\,d\varphi}{R^2-2Rr\cos(	heta-\varphi)+r^2},\&\qquad 0\le r<R,\end{aligned}$$ which tends continuously to the continuous boundary data $g$ as $r	o R^-$. Sign convention: here $\Gamma=+ rac1{2\pi}\ln r$ and $
u$ is the outward normal; if the fundamental solution is taken with the opposite sign, the representation changes sign accordingly.

formulas.note: 二维拉普拉斯方程；满足它的函数称为调和函数。高维修成 $\Delta u=\sum_{i}u_{x_ix_i}=0$。
formulas.noteEn: Laplace's equation in two dimensions; solutions are harmonic functions. In higher dimensions the sum runs over all $u_{x_ix_i}$.

formulas.note: 极坐标形式；圆域、扇形域、环形域上的边值问题用它最方便，也是分离变量法的起点。
formulas.noteEn: The polar form; it is the natural tool on disks, sectors and annuli and the starting point of separation of variables.

formulas.note: 二维基本解：$r>0$ 时调和。以它为核并结合边界条件可以构造 Green 函数。
formulas.noteEn: The two-dimensional fundamental solution, harmonic for $r>0$; used as a kernel together with boundary data to construct Green's functions.

formulas.note: 均值性质：调和函数在一点的值等于围绕它的圆周上的平均值，也等于对应圆盘上的平均值（两式等价）。
formulas.noteEn: Mean value property: the value at a point equals both the average over any circle around it and the average over the enclosed disk, the two statements being equivalent.

formulas.note: Dirichlet 边值问题：内部求调和函数、边界上取给定数据 $g$。$g$ 连续时解唯一且稳定；Neumann 问题给 $\partial u/\partial n$，Robin 给 $\partial u/\partial n+\sigma u$。
formulas.noteEn: The Dirichlet boundary value problem: find a harmonic function inside $\Omega$ taking the prescribed values $g$ on the boundary. The solution is unique and stable for continuous $g$; the Neumann problem prescribes $\partial u/\partial n$ and the Robin problem $\partial u/\partial n+\sigma u$.

properties: 解是调和函数：在区域内部无限次可微、实解析；奇异只可能出现在区域边界或被挖掉的点（如基本解的原点）。
最大值原理：非常数调和函数在区域内部不能取得最大值或最小值，极值必在边界取到；对 Dirichlet 问题立即推出解的唯一性。
均值性质：$u(\mathbf{x}_0)$ 等于以 $\mathbf{x}_0$ 为心的圆周或圆盘上的平均值，由它可以推出最大值原理。
椭圆型方程的提法：只给边界条件（无初始条件）；Neumann 问题有解的必要条件是 $\oint_{\partial\Omega}\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}\,ds=0$，且解只确定到相差一个常数。
稳定性：由最大值原理有 $\sup_{\Omega}|u|\le\sup_{\partial\Omega}|g|$，边界数据的微小改变只引起解的微小改变，边值问题是适定的。
propertiesEn: Solutions are harmonic: infinitely differentiable and real analytic inside the domain; singularities can only occur on the boundary or at removed points such as the origin in the fundamental solution.
Maximum principle: a nonconstant harmonic function has no interior maximum or minimum, so extremes occur on the boundary; uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem follows immediately.
Mean value property: $u(\mathbf{x}_0)$ equals the average of $u$ over any circle or disk centred at $\mathbf{x}_0$, and this implies the maximum principle.

Formulation for an elliptic equation: boundary data only, no initial conditions; the Neumann problem requires the compatibility condition $\oint_{\partial\Omega}\frac{\partial u}{\partial n}\,ds=0$ and determines $u$ only up to an additive constant.

Stability: the maximum principle gives $\sup_{\Omega}|u|\le\sup_{\partial\Omega}|g|$, so small changes in the boundary data produce small changes in the solution — the boundary value problem is well posed.

examples.problem: 验证 $u(x,y)=x^{2}-y^{2}$ 是调和函数，并给出它在单位圆边界上的值。
examples.solution:
求二阶偏导：$u_{xx}=2$，$u_{yy}=-2$，因此 $\Delta u=2+(-2)=0$，$u$ 调和。在单位圆上 $x=\cos	heta$、$y=\sin	heta$，边界值为

$$u(1,	heta)=\cos^{2}	heta-\sin^{2}	heta=\cos 2	heta.$$

所以它恰好是 Dirichlet 问题 $\Delta u=0$（$r<1$）、$u(1,	heta)=\cos 2	heta$ 的解，用极坐标写就是 $u=r^{2}\cos 2	heta$。

examples.problem: 验证 $u(x,y)=\ln r$（$r>0$）是调和函数；它能作为单位圆盘（含原点）上的 Dirichlet 边值问题的解吗？
examples.solution: 用极坐标形式：$u=\ln r$ 只依赖 $r$，逐项计算得 $\dfrac{1}{r}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial r}\left(r\cdot\dfrac{1}{r}\right)=\dfrac{1}{r}\cdot 0=0$，角度方向导数为零，所以 $r>0$ 时 $\Delta u=0$，$u$ 在除原点外处处调和。但它在原点奇异（$r\to 0$ 时 $u\to-\infty$），不是圆盘内部处处有定义的函数，因此不能充当含原点区域的 Dirichlet 问题的解：边界数据 $g(\theta)=u(1,\theta)=0$，由唯一性解应是 $u\equiv 0$。$\ln r$ 的真正身份是二维基本解，用于构造 Green 函数。

expression.note: 稳态（不含时间）的椭圆型方程，解是调和函数，只需边界条件。
expression.noteEn: A steady-state elliptic equation with no time variable; its solutions are harmonic functions fixed by boundary data alone.

separation-of-variables.definition:
分离变量法是求解**有界区域**上**线性齐次**偏微分方程（配齐次边界条件）的基本方法。它把求解偏微分方程的问题化为求解若干常微分方程的问题，基本想法是假设解能写成「只含空间变量的函数」与「只含时间变量的函数」的乘积：
$$u(x,t)=X(x)T(t).$$

以长为 $L$ 的杆上的热传导方程 $u_t=a^2u_{xx}$ 为例，代入并整理后可把含 $x$ 的项与含 $t$ 的项分离到等号两侧；两侧恒等就要求它们同为常数，称为**分离常数**，记成 $-\lambda$：
$$\frac{X''}{X}=\frac{T'}{a^2T}=-\lambda.$$
于是问题化为一个关于 $X$ 的**特征值问题**和一个关于 $T$ 的常微分方程：$X''+\lambda X=0$ 与 $T'+\lambda a^2T=0$（波动方程对应 $T''+\lambda a^2T=0$）。

**关键一步**是把齐次边界条件转移到 $X$ 上：由 $u(0,t)=X(0)T(t)=0$（对一切 $t$ 成立，且 $T\not\equiv0$）得 $X(0)=0$，同理 $X(L)=0$。此时 $X''+\lambda X=0$，$X(0)=X(L)=0$ 只有对离散的**特征值**才有非平凡解：
$$\lambda_n=\left(\frac{n\pi}{L}\right)^2,\qquad X_n(x)=\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L},\qquad n=1,2,3,\dots$$
注意 $n$ 从 1 开始——$n=0$ 给出 $\sin 0\equiv0$，是零解，必须排除；而 $\lambda_n$ 是 $(n\pi/L)^2$ 而不是 $n\pi/L$。

最后把各模式叠加（线性齐次问题的解之和仍是解）：$u=\sum_{n\ge1}b_nX_n(x)T_n(t)$。代入初始条件 $u(x,0)=\varphi(x)$，利用正弦系的正交性逐一「筛」出系数：
$$b_n=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^L\varphi(x)\,\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx.$$
整个流程可以概括为：**设乘积解 → 分离变量 → 齐次边界条件定特征值问题 → 叠加 → 初值条件定系数**。
separation-of-variables.definitionEn:
Separation of variables is the standard device for solving **linear homogeneous** PDEs on a **bounded domain** with homogeneous boundary conditions. It trades a PDE for several ODEs by looking for solutions that factor into a purely spatial part and a purely temporal part:
$$u(x,t)=X(x)T(t).$$

For the heat equation $u_t=a^2u_{xx}$ on a rod of length $L$, substitution and rearrangement place every $x$-dependent term on one side and every $t$-dependent term on the other; equality forces both sides to equal a constant, the **separation constant**, written $-\lambda$:
$$\frac{X''}{X}=\frac{T'}{a^2T}=-\lambda.$$
The problem then splits into an **eigenvalue problem** for $X$ and an ODE for $T$: $X''+\lambda X=0$ together with $T'+\lambda a^2T=0$ (the wave equation gives $T''+\lambda a^2T=0$).

**The crucial step** transfers the homogeneous boundary conditions to $X$: from $u(0,t)=X(0)T(t)=0$ for all $t$ (with $T\not\equiv0$) we get $X(0)=0$, and likewise $X(L)=0$. The problem $X''+\lambda X=0$, $X(0)=X(L)=0$ has nontrivial solutions only for the discrete **eigenvalues**
$$\lambda_n=\left(\frac{n\pi}{L}\right)^2,\qquad X_n(x)=\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L},\qquad n=1,2,3,\dots$$
The index starts at $n=1$ because $n=0$ gives the zero solution; note that $\lambda_n$ is $(n\pi/L)^2$, not $n\pi/L$.

Finally, superpose the modes (sums of solutions of a linear homogeneous problem are again solutions), $u=\sum_{n\ge1}b_nX_n(x)T_n(t)$, and impose $u(x,0)=\varphi(x)$. Orthogonality of the sine system isolates the coefficients one by one:
$$b_n=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^L\varphi(x)\,\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx.$$
In short: **product ansatz → separate the variables → homogeneous boundary conditions give the eigenvalue problem → superpose → initial conditions fix the coefficients**.
derivation: 设区域为 $(0,L)$，考虑线性齐次方程 $u_t=a^2u_{xx}$（热方程）或 $u_{tt}=a^2u_{xx}$（波动方程），并配齐次边界条件。设乘积解 $$u(x,t)=X(x)T(t),$$ 且 $X,T$ 不恒为零。代入热方程得 $XT'=a^2X''T$；在 $XT\ne0$ 处除以 $a^2XT$：$$\frac{T'}{a^2T}=\frac{X''}{X}.$$ 左端只依赖 $t$，右端只依赖 $x$，故二者必为同一常数，记作 $-\lambda$。于是 $$X''+\lambda X=0,\qquad T'+\lambda a^2T=0.$$ 波动方程同理给出 $T''+\lambda a^2T=0$。若 $X$ 或 $T$ 恒为零，只得到零解，不能提供特征模式，故予排除。

齐次边界条件转移到 $X$：以两端 Dirichlet $u(0,t)=u(L,t)=0$ 为例，$$X(0)T(t)=0,\qquad X(L)T(t)=0$$ 对一切 $t>0$。若 $T\equiv0$ 则 $u\equiv0$；否则存在 $t_0$ 使 $T(t_0)\ne0$，故 $X(0)=X(L)=0$。类似地，Neumann 条件 $u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t)=0$ 转为 $X'(0)=X'(L)=0$；Robin 条件 $\alpha u+\beta u_x=0$ 转为 $\alpha X+\beta X'=0$。非齐次边界条件不能直接转移，需先作代换 $u=v+w$，其中 $w$ 满足给定的非齐次边界数据，把 $v$ 的边界化为齐次。

解 Dirichlet 特征值问题 $$X''+\lambda X=0,\qquad X(0)=X(L)=0,\quad L>0.$$ 分三种情形。若 $\lambda<0$，写 $\lambda=-\mu^2$（$\mu>0$），$X=A\cosh\mu x+B\sinh\mu x$；由 $X(0)=0$ 得 $A=0$，由 $X(L)=B\sinh\mu L=0$ 且 $\sinh\mu L\ne0$ 得 $B=0$，只有零解。若 $\lambda=0$，$X=A+Bx$，两端条件同样迫使 $A=B=0$。若 $\lambda>0$，写 $\lambda=\omega^2$（$\omega>0$），$X=A\cos\omega x+B\sin\omega x$；$X(0)=0$ 给 $A=0$，$X(L)=B\sin\omega L=0$。非零解要求 $B\ne0$，故 $\sin\omega L=0$，即 $\omega L=n\pi$，$n=1,2,\dots$。于是 $$\lambda_n=\left(\frac{n\pi}{L}\right)^2,\qquad X_n(x)=\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L},\qquad n=1,2,\dots$$ $n=0$ 给出零函数，必须排除。

时间方程与叠加：热方程中 $T_n'+\lambda_na^2T_n=0$，故 $$T_n(t)=e^{-\lambda_na^2t}=e^{-(n\pi a/L)^2t},$$ 乘积解为 $$u_n(x,t)=\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,e^{-(n\pi a/L)^2t}.$$ 波动方程中 $T_n''+\lambda_na^2T_n=0$，故 $$T_n(t)=A_n\cos(\omega_nt)+B_n\sin(\omega_nt),\qquad \omega_n=\frac{n\pi a}{L},$$ 乘积解是驻波。有限个 $u_n$ 的线性组合仍满足方程与齐次边界条件，这是线性齐次方程的叠加原理。无限和 $u=\sum_n c_nu_n$ 形式上满足方程，但要成为经典解，必须保证逐项求导后的级数收敛：热方程在 $t\ge\delta>0$ 上因指数因子可任意次逐项求导；波动方程没有衰减因子，需要 $\sum_n n^2|c_n|$ 等收敛，通常由初值的光滑性与相容性保证。

Fourier 系数：以热方程 Dirichlet 问题为例，初始条件为 $$u(x,0)=\varphi(x)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}.$$ 正弦系满足正交性 $$\int_0^L\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\sin\frac{m\pi x}{L}\,dx=\frac L2\delta_{nm}.$$ 两边乘 $\sin(m\pi x/L)$ 并在 $(0,L)$ 上积分，只有 $n=m$ 项留下，故 $$b_n=\frac2L\int_0^L\varphi(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx.$$ 若 $\varphi$ 分段光滑，其正弦级数在连续点收敛到 $\varphi(x)$，在跳跃点收敛到 $\frac12[\varphi(x^+)+\varphi(x^-)]$，并在任何不含跳跃点的闭子区间上一致收敛。波动方程还要用 $u_t(x,0)=\psi(x)$ 定另一组系数：$A_n$ 由 $\varphi$ 给出，$B_n=\frac{2}{n\pi a}\int_0^L\psi(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}dx$。

收敛性与适用范围：热方程只需 $\varphi\in L^2(0,L)$（或分段连续）即可定义级数解；对任意 $\delta>0$，因 $\lambda_n\ge\pi^2/L^2$，$\sum_n\lambda_n^k e^{-\lambda_na^2\delta}$ 收敛，故 $u\in C^\infty((0,L)\times(\delta,\infty))$，$t>0$ 后立即光滑。波动方程要得到 $C^2$ 经典解，可用如下充分条件：$\varphi\in C^3$、$\psi\in C^2$，并满足与边界相容的端点条件 $\varphi(0)=\varphi(L)=\varphi''(0)=\varphi''(L)=0$、$\psi(0)=\psi(L)=0$，以保证逐项求导两次后的级数一致收敛；条件不足时级数可能只在 $L^2$ 意义下收敛，只是弱解。无论哪种情形，分离变量先给出形式解，必须单独验证收敛与逐项求导；边界条件决定特征函数系（Dirichlet 用正弦，Neumann 用余弦），不能混用。非齐次方程或非齐次边界需先齐次化或用特征函数展开。
derivationEn: Take the domain $(0,L)$ and a linear homogeneous equation, either $u_t=a^2u_{xx}$ (heat) or $u_{tt}=a^2u_{xx}$ (wave), with homogeneous boundary conditions. Seek a product solution $$u(x,t)=X(x)T(t),$$ with $X,T$ not identically zero. Substituting into the heat equation gives $XT'=a^2X''T$; dividing by $a^2XT$ where $XT\ne0$, $$\frac{T'}{a^2T}=\frac{X''}{X}.$$ The left side depends only on $t$ and the right only on $x$, so both equal a constant, written $-\lambda$. Hence $$X''+\lambda X=0,\qquad T'+\lambda a^2T=0.$$ The wave equation similarly gives $T''+\lambda a^2T=0$. If $X$ or $T$ vanishes identically, only the zero solution results and no eigenmode is obtained, so such factors are excluded.

Transfer homogeneous boundary conditions to $X$: for Dirichlet conditions $u(0,t)=u(L,t)=0$, $$X(0)T(t)=0,\qquad X(L)T(t)=0$$ for all $t>0$. If $T\equiv0$ then $u\equiv0$; otherwise some $t_0$ has $T(t_0)\ne0$, so $X(0)=X(L)=0$. Likewise, Neumann conditions $u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t)=0$ become $X'(0)=X'(L)=0$, and Robin conditions $\alpha u+\beta u_x=0$ become $\alpha X+\beta X'=0$. Nonhomogeneous boundary conditions cannot be transferred directly; one first writes $u=v+w$, where $w$ matches the prescribed boundary data, making the boundary conditions for $v$ homogeneous.

Solve the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem $$X''+\lambda X=0,\qquad X(0)=X(L)=0,\quad L>0.$$ There are three cases. If $\lambda<0$, write $\lambda=-\mu^2$ with $\mu>0$ and $X=A\cosh\mu x+B\sinh\mu x$; $X(0)=0$ gives $A=0$, and $X(L)=B\sinh\mu L=0$ with $\sinh\mu L\ne0$ gives $B=0$, so only the zero solution exists. If $\lambda=0$, $X=A+Bx$, and the endpoint conditions again force $A=B=0$. If $\lambda>0$, write $\lambda=\omega^2$ with $\omega>0$ and $X=A\cos\omega x+B\sin\omega x$; $X(0)=0$ gives $A=0$, and $X(L)=B\sin\omega L=0$. A nonzero solution needs $B\ne0$, hence $\sin\omega L=0$, i.e. $\omega L=n\pi$ for $n=1,2,\dots$. Therefore $$\lambda_n=\left(\frac{n\pi}{L}\right)^2,\qquad X_n(x)=\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L},\qquad n=1,2,\dots,$$ and $n=0$ gives the zero function, so it is excluded.

Time equations and superposition: for the heat equation $T_n'+\lambda_na^2T_n=0$, so $$T_n(t)=e^{-\lambda_na^2t}=e^{-(n\pi a/L)^2t},$$ and the product solutions are $$u_n(x,t)=\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,e^{-(n\pi a/L)^2t}.$$ For the wave equation $T_n''+\lambda_na^2T_n=0$, so $$T_n(t)=A_n\cos(\omega_nt)+B_n\sin(\omega_nt),\qquad \omega_n=\frac{n\pi a}{L},$$ and the product solutions are standing waves. Finite linear combinations of the $u_n$ still satisfy the equation and the homogeneous boundary conditions—this is superposition for a linear homogeneous problem. The infinite sum $u=\sum_n c_nu_n$ formally satisfies the equation, but to be a classical solution the differentiated series must converge: for the heat equation the exponential factor permits termwise differentiation of every order on $t\ge\delta>0$; for the wave equation there is no decay factor, and one needs convergence of $\sum_n n^2|c_n|$ and similar series, usually ensured by smoothness and compatibility of the initial data.

Fourier coefficients: for the Dirichlet heat problem, the initial condition is $$u(x,0)=\varphi(x)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}.$$ The sine system is orthogonal: $$\int_0^L\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\sin\frac{m\pi x}{L}\,dx=\frac L2\delta_{nm}.$$ Multiplying by $\sin(m\pi x/L)$ and integrating over $(0,L)$ leaves only the $n=m$ term, so $$b_n=\frac2L\int_0^L\varphi(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx.$$ If $\varphi$ is piecewise smooth, its sine series converges to $\varphi(x)$ at continuity points and to $\frac12[\varphi(x^+)+\varphi(x^-)]$ at jumps, uniformly on any closed subinterval containing no jump. For the wave equation the data $u_t(x,0)=\psi(x)$ determine a second set of coefficients: $A_n$ comes from $\varphi$, while $B_n=\frac{2}{n\pi a}\int_0^L\psi(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}dx$.

Convergence and scope: for the heat equation it suffices that $\varphi\in L^2(0,L)$ (or piecewise continuous) to define the series; for every $\delta>0$, since $\lambda_n\ge\pi^2/L^2$, the series $\sum_n\lambda_n^k e^{-\lambda_na^2\delta}$ converges, so $u\in C^\infty((0,L)\times(\delta,\infty))$ and is instantly smooth for $t>0$. For a $C^2$ classical solution of the wave equation, a sufficient set of conditions is $\varphi\in C^3$, $\psi\in C^2$, together with the compatible endpoint conditions $\varphi(0)=\varphi(L)=\varphi''(0)=\varphi''(L)=0$, $\psi(0)=\psi(L)=0$, which make the twice-differentiated series converge uniformly; without enough smoothness the series may converge only in $L^2$ and represent a weak solution. In either case separation of variables first produces a formal solution, and convergence and termwise differentiation must be checked separately; the boundary conditions determine the eigenfunction system (sine for Dirichlet, cosine for Neumann), and the two must not be mixed. Nonhomogeneous equations or boundary data require homogenisation or eigenfunction expansion.

formulas.noteEn: The product ansatz: a solution that factors into a function of $x$ alone times a function of $t$ alone.

formulas.noteEn: Homogeneous boundary conditions quantize the separation constant; $n=0$ gives only the zero solution, so the index starts at 1.

formulas.noteEn: The separated solution of the heat equation: mode $n$ decays exponentially at rate $\lambda_na^2=(n\pi a/L)^2$.

formulas.noteEn: The coefficient determined by the initial condition $u(x,0)=\varphi(x)$ and the orthogonality of the sine system.

properties: 适用条件是**线性齐次**方程加**齐次**边界条件；非齐次方程可用特征函数展开，非齐次边界要先通过代换化为齐次。
分离常数 $\lambda$ 由边界条件决定：两端狄利克雷条件下只有 $\lambda>0$ 有非平凡解，特征值 $\lambda_n=(n\pi/L)^2$ 按 $n^2$ 增长。
特征函数 $\sin(n\pi x/L)$ 在 $[0,L]$ 上两两正交且构成完备系，可以展开相当广泛的初值函数。
叠加原理成立：各乘积解的有限或（收敛的）无穷线性组合仍然满足方程与齐次边界条件。
长期形态由低阶模式主导：热传导中高阶模式先衰减、解趋于 0（或有源时趋于最低模式），波动中各模式保持能量、只振荡不衰减。
propertiesEn: It applies to **linear homogeneous** equations with **homogeneous** boundary conditions; nonhomogeneous equations are handled by eigenfunction expansion, and nonhomogeneous boundary data are first reduced to the homogeneous case.

The separation constant $\lambda$ is fixed by the boundary conditions: with Dirichlet conditions at both ends only $\lambda>0$ gives nontrivial solutions, and the eigenvalues $\lambda_n=(n\pi/L)^2$ grow like $n^2$.
The eigenfunctions $\sin(n\pi x/L)$ are pairwise orthogonal on $[0,L]$ and complete, so a wide class of initial data can be expanded in them.
Superposition holds: finite or (convergent) infinite linear combinations of the product solutions still satisfy the equation and the homogeneous boundary conditions.

Long-time behavior is dominated by low modes: in heat flow high modes decay first and the solution tends to $0$ (or to the lowest mode with forcing), while wave modes keep their energy and merely oscillate.

examples.problem:
用分离变量法求解热传导方程的初边值问题
$$u_t=a^2u_{xx},\quad 0<x<L,\ t>0;\qquad u(0,t)=u(L,t)=0;\qquad u(x,0)=\varphi(x).$$
examples.solution:
设 $u=X(x)T(t)$，代入得 $X''+\lambda X=0$ 与 $T'+\lambda a^2T=0$。由齐次边界条件得特征值问题 $X''+\lambda X=0$，$X(0)=X(L)=0$，其解为 $\lambda_n=(n\pi/L)^2$，$X_n(x)=\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}$，$n=1,2,3,\dots$，于是 $T_n(t)=e^{-\lambda_na^2t}=e^{-(n\pi a/L)^2t}$，叠加得
$$u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}b_n\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}e^{-(n\pi a/L)^2t}.$$
再由 $u(x,0)=\varphi(x)$ 与正交性 $\int_0^L\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\sin\frac{m\pi x}{L}dx=\frac{L}{2}\delta_{mn}$ 得 $b_n=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^L\varphi(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}dx$。（若记 $L=1$，衰减因子就是 $e^{-n^2\pi^2a^2t}$。）

examples.problem: 求解 $u_t=u_{xx}$（$0<x<1$），$u(0,t)=u(1,t)=0$，$u(x,0)=x(1-x)$，写出级数解并指出长期衰减速率。
examples.solution:
这里 $L=1,a=1$，$\lambda_n=n^2\pi^2$。系数为 $b_n=2\int_0^1x(1-x)\sin(n\pi x)\,dx$：$n$ 为偶数时积分为 0，$n$ 为奇数时 $b_n=\frac{8}{n^3\pi^3}$。于是
$$u(x,t)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{8}{(2k+1)^3\pi^3}\,\sin\big((2k+1)\pi x\big)\,e^{-(2k+1)^2\pi^2t}.$$
当 $t\to\infty$，$u\to0$，且衰减速率由最低模式 $n=1$ 决定，约为 $e^{-\pi^2t}$。（把级数在 $t=0$ 处取前 20 项，即可看到它逼近抛物线 $x(1-x)$。）

sturm-liouville.definition:
施图姆-刘维尔（Sturm–Liouville）问题是分离变量法背后的一般理论框架。把二阶线性方程写成**自伴形式**
$$(p(x)y')'+[\lambda\rho(x)-q(x)]y=0,\qquad a<x<b,$$
再加上**分离型边界条件**（如 $y(a)=y(b)=0$，或一般的 $\alpha y+\beta y'=0$ 且两端各自成条件），就构成一个施图姆-刘维尔问题。这里 $p>0$ 是「刚度」系数，$\rho>0$ 是权函数，$q$ 是位势。当 $p,\rho,q$ 在有限区间上连续、$p>0$、$\rho>0$ 时称为**正则**问题。

为什么要把它单独拿出来？因为它把「特征值问题」从具体方程中抽象出来，并保证了一整套与对称矩阵完全平行的定理：特征值全是**实数**，可以从小到大排成一列 $\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\lambda_3<\cdots$ 而且**趋于无穷**；不同特征值的特征函数关于权 $\rho$ **正交**：
$$\int_a^b\rho(x)y_m(x)y_n(x)\,dx=0\qquad(m\ne n);$$
并且特征函数系在相应的函数空间中**完备**，任意（分段光滑的）函数都可以按它展开成广义傅里叶级数。正弦系 $\sin(n\pi x/L)$、余弦系、勒让德多项式、贝塞尔函数，都是它的特例。

正交性的来源是**自伴性**（拉格朗日恒等式）：对两个特征函数成立
$$\left[p(y_m'y_n-y_my_n')\right]'=(\lambda_n-\lambda_m)\rho\,y_my_n,$$
两端积分后边界项被分离边界条件消去，于是 $(\lambda_n-\lambda_m)\int\rho y_my_n=0$。这套理论解释了为什么分离变量法总能把解写成级数：正交性负责逐一求出系数，完备性保证级数能表示一般的初值。
sturm-liouville.definitionEn:
The Sturm–Liouville (SL) problem is the general framework behind separation of variables. Writing a second-order linear equation in **self-adjoint form**
$$(p(x)y')'+[\lambda\rho(x)-q(x)]y=0,\qquad a<x<b,$$
and adjoining **separated boundary conditions** (for instance $y(a)=y(b)=0$, or conditions of the form $\alpha y+\beta y'=0$ at each endpoint) gives an SL problem. Here $p>0$ plays the role of a stiffness coefficient, $\rho>0$ is the weight, and $q$ is a potential. When $p,\rho,q$ are continuous on a finite interval with $p>0,\rho>0$ the problem is called **regular**.

The abstraction pays off because it carries an array of theorems exactly parallel to those for symmetric matrices: the eigenvalues are all **real** and can be arranged in an increasing sequence $\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\lambda_3<\cdots$ with $\lambda_n\to\infty$; eigenfunctions belonging to different eigenvalues are **orthogonal with weight $\rho$**:
$$\int_a^b\rho(x)y_m(x)y_n(x)\,dx=0\qquad(m\ne n);$$
and the eigenfunction system is **complete**, so any (piecewise smooth) function expands in a generalized Fourier series. The sine system $\sin(n\pi x/L)$, cosines, Legendre polynomials and Bessel functions are all special cases.

The source of orthogonality is **self-adjointness** (Lagrange's identity): for two eigenfunctions
$$\left[p(y_m'y_n-y_my_n')\right]'=(\lambda_n-\lambda_m)\rho\,y_my_n,$$
and after integration the boundary terms vanish by the separated boundary conditions, giving $(\lambda_n-\lambda_m)\int\rho y_my_n=0$. This is precisely why separation of variables always produces series expansions: orthogonality computes the coefficients one at a time, and completeness represents the general initial data.
derivation: 设 $p\in C^1[a,b]$、$q,\rho\in C[a,b]$，且 $p(x)>0$、$\rho(x)>0$。施图姆–刘维尔方程写成自伴形式 $$(p(x)y')'+[\lambda\rho(x)-q(x)]y=0.$$ 令 $L[y]=(py')'-qy$，则方程即 $L[y]=-\lambda\rho y$。对两个 $C^2$ 函数 $y_m,y_n$ 直接求导可验证拉格朗日恒等式 $$y_mL[y_n]-y_nL[y_m]=\frac{d}{dx}\left[p(y_my_n'-y_ny_m')\right].$$ 右端是全导数，这是自伴性的微分形式：$L$ 关于无权内积 $\int_a^b fg\,dx$ 对称；等价地，$T=\frac1\rho L$ 关于带权内积 $\langle f,g\rangle_\rho=\int_a^b\rho fg\,dx$ 对称。积分后唯一的障碍是边界项。

设边界条件为分离型：$$\begin{aligned}\alpha y(a)+\beta y'(a)&=0,\\ \gamma y(b)+\delta y'(b)&=0.\end{aligned}$$ 其中 $\alpha,\beta$ 不同时为零，$\gamma,\delta$ 不同时为零，系数取实数。若 $y_m,y_n$ 都满足同一端的条件，则该端的两个向量 $(y,y')$ 同属于一条过原点的直线，行列式 $y_my_n'-y_ny_m'$ 为零，故 $$p(y_my_n'-y_ny_m')\Big|_a^b=0.$$ 把拉格朗日恒等式在 $[a,b]$ 上积分，并使用 $L[y_k]=-\lambda_k\rho y_k$，得 $$(\lambda_m-\lambda_n)\int_a^b\rho y_my_n\,dx=0.$$ 若 $\lambda_m\ne\lambda_n$，立即得到带权正交。

特征值全为实数。若允许复值函数，设 $y$ 是特征值 $\lambda$ 的特征函数，用 $\bar y$ 乘方程 $L[y]=-\lambda\rho y$ 并积分：$$\int_a^b[(py')'\bar y-q|y|^2]dx=-\lambda\int_a^b\rho|y|^2dx.$$ 对第一项分部积分得 $$\int_a^b p|y'|^2dx+\int_a^b q|y|^2dx-\big[p y'\bar y\big]_a^b=\lambda\int_a^b\rho|y|^2dx.$$ 在分离型实系数边界条件下，边界项 $p y'\bar y$ 是实数（Dirichlet/Neumann 时为零，Robin 时由 $y'=-\alpha y/\beta$ 化为实数），且分母 $\int\rho|y|^2>0$，故 $\lambda$ 等于一个实数，特征值必实。
